_readBy: Read by the scripts: `android.*`, `devices`, `managedDevices` and `campaign`. Everything else documents the plan for the humans and the agent filling CAMPAIGN.md. Secrets never go in this file
_campaign: optional: the name the device claim uses to tell campaigns apart. Without it, the git root of this file's folder — so a second config for the same campaign (another app id for the release build) is still the same campaign.

app.name: My App
app.reference: https://example.com/app  (REF: the implementation that is the full list of what the domain supports)

android._packagePrefix: optional. What counts as 'the app' in the accessibility tree and the crash log. Without it, exactly `package`. Prefer a LIST of exact names to count several variants as one app: ["com.example.myapp", "com.example.myapp.debug"]. A bare prefix string still works, but it is REFUSED when more than one installed package matches it — the vendor's other apps would read as this one's, and a flow driven in one would count as the other's.
android._secretKeys: optional: words that are credentials in THIS product — an NFC card id that signs someone in, an employee number. db, file and log hide values whose key contains one.
android._databases: alias → a SQLite file: a bare name is inside the app's databases/ folder, a path with / is relative to its data folder (WorkManager's queue lives in no_backup/). `ui.py db <alias>` refuses a name that is not listed here, unless it is itself a path (it has a / or ends in .db). `ui.py files` shows where the stores really are.
android._files: alias → any other file the app keeps, relative to its data folder. `ui.py file <alias>` prints text with secret-looking values hidden, and refuses to print binary (a Proto DataStore): copy it with --out for the project's own reader.

ios._readBy: nothing yet — the shape a harness/ios/ is expected to read
ios._stores: alias → path relative to the app's data container (or an App Group container)

web._readBy: nothing yet — the shape a harness/web/ is expected to read

devices._note: alias → the platform's identifier: `avd:<name>` for an Android emulator (its serial is only the console port it got at boot, so it is looked up on every command — start emulators with -port <even number>), an adb serial for a physical phone; a simulator UDID for iOS; a browser profile or viewport name for web. Once this lists any device, the scripts refuse every device that is not on the list (keys starting with _ are ignored).

_managedDevices: aliases or serials of devices that are not the campaign's to alter (a managed work phone, someone's own phone): rotate, size, demo, clear-crashes and net.sh on/off/slow/full refuse on them unless --allow-device-change / QA_ALLOW_DEVICE_CHANGE=1.

server._note: the test server agreed at setup (SKILL.md §2.1) — whether it is a disposable copy or a shared one, and whose data it holds. `net.sh reach` checks it from the DEVICE with urlFromDevice. This example is a server on this computer, reached after `adb reverse tcp:8080 tcp:8080`: 10.0.2.2 answers the device's SHELL but the app's own uid timed out on it (R10). A server on the LAN or a VPN: the address the DEVICE resolves, which may not be the one this computer uses.

session._note: for the plan, not executed by the scripts: the command that logs a device in WITHOUT anyone typing a password (R11). {account} is A, B or C. If no such command can exist (an iCloud sign-in), the sign-in is a one-time user-queue item (R2).

fixtures._markerField: the field that carries the prefix. Pick one the server stores as sent: create one fixture, read it back through the API, and move the prefix (URL, tag, description) if the server rewrote it.
permanentDeletes: for the plan: which of your backend's deletes are permanent rather than a trash
